newsitem.title: USA: Comm Ed offers early retirement to 1,500 people.
newsitem.headline: Comm Ed offers early retirement to 1,500 people.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co said Monday it offered early retirement packages to 1,500 of its 16,700 full and part-time employees in a move to reduce costs.
"As deregulation comes on the horizon, it's necessary to cut costs to be more competitive in the future," a Commonwealth Edison spokesman said.
Employees were informed July 16 about the offers and can accept the offers between July 28 and December 5, he told Reuters confirming a report in the August 4 issue of Crain's Chicago Business.
Terms of the early retirement packages will be determined by a formula based on years of service, he said.

Commonwealth Edison, a subsidiary of Unicom Corp, did not disclose how many employees it expects to accept the offer. Historically, when such plans are offered, usually 10 percent to 15 percent accept, he noted.
Shares of Unicom closed up 1/16 to 22-13/16.
